DNNs are not the best choice for SC and polyphony AED tasks.
for SC, DNNs and TDNNs outperform GMMs and that for AED, GMMs outperform DNNs.

the following aspects: 1 the use of DNNs and time-delay NNs for SC; 2 the use of GFB features in conjunction with DNNs and GMMs for SC; and 3 the use of DNBs and GMM-HMMs for AED.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DNNs and time-delay NNs are promising approaches for the considered tasks, but that the current state of the art is not yet reached by DNNs and TDNNs.
the use of DNNs in SC and AED systems is promising, but that the benefits of DNNs are not always clear.
the DNNs are not yet the best choice in the DCASE'06 challenge, but that DNNs are a promising approach and that their performance can be expected to improve in the near future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DNNs and TDNNs are not yet suitable for acoustic scene classification and event detection.
DNNs can improve performance for SC but not for AED, which is in contrast to the results from DCASE'16 task 1 and 3.
the proposed DNN-based systems for the DCASE' 16 challenge tasks do not outperform the baseline systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of DNNs is beneficial for SC, but for AED, the use of DMMs is more appropriate.
for both SC and AED, the performance of NNs is still behind traditional approaches, which are based on GMMs and HMMs, respectively.
DNN-based approaches are very promising for SC and AED.
